questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I choose to study in Paris because I have a big love for the city and have always dreamed of living there.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was very easy. My home university was very helpful and available to answer questions and solving any issues.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I did not have any personal assistance, however, there were a group of students from my host university who made a WhatsApp group for all the Erasmus students to use when in need for help.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Luckily I knew a person who was on an exchange program in Paris the semester before me so I could take over his rental agreement when he finished his semester.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: I have heard there are a lot of scammers on the rental market so try to find apartments with official rental agencies.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: It was very easy for me because I chose to follow the same courses that I had chosen before arrival

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: There was always an LLM coordinator and a Erasmus Law coordinator available at the university to answer any questions. Additionally, there was also a group of local students who made a WhatsApp group to all the Erasmus students which we also could use for any questions.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got all the classes I wanted.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: My experience was that a lot of local students were really helpful so my advice is to be in contact with some students from the host university as well.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Overall the level was quite low. My experience was that the courses were not difficult in a legal way. Instead, most of the exams were really about memorizing definitions of different terms, and not solving legal cases like I personally was used to do in UCPH.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The level of teaching was also very low compared to UCPH. Many professors in the law courses did not have a law degree - instead most teachers had a background in political science or international relations. Therefore, the courses often had a political angle and not legally heavy. Furthermore, some teaches were very unenthusiastic. For example, in some courses the teachers just read out loud some power point slides, did not really answer questions and always finished one hour early which was quite annoying when I personally had a 3 hour travel time back and forth to the university. Furthermore, some teachers were very traditional in their way of teaching. I had a teacher who did not use nor a whiteboard or power points, and instead just talked about the different subjects without any structure. This made it really hard to follow his teaching especially because the pensum for the exams was the teachers words - there were no pensum books at all.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Introduction to European Union Law (LLM course), Contract Law (LLM course), Argumentation and Negotiation, Business Law and Criminal Law and Procedure.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would recommend both the Criminal Law and the Introduction to the European Union Law because of the teacher. He was very structural and it was easy to follow his teaching. I would recommend Argumentation and Negotiation to students who would like a break from the legal courses as it was very easy and was mostly about creating and analyzing speeches.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Paris is an expensive city to live in so generally going out to eat, shop etc. can cost a lot.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Most museums are free for EU citizens under 26. Transportation was also less expensive than I expected.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There is a lot of different social activities - both sports and cultural activities. However, I did not join any of the activities because I lived far away from the university.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: There is a lot of things to do in Paris. I therefore recommend going to museums, different restaurants, flea markets etc. The students at the host university were really helpful with arranging trips to different museums, the Eiffel Tower etc.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: I spent two weekends travelling to other places in France - Normandy and Marseille - which I would really recommend. It is very easy to take the train from Paris to a lot of different cities in France. Since they have high-speed trains (TGV) it only took me 3 hours to travel from Paris to Marseille - and it takes around 9 hours by car.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was very easy. I found many people to be very helpful.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: There was a big Erasmus group at my university so I did not really get to socialize a lot with the local students. However, they were really helpful.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: I found some teachers to be very traditional in their way of teaching. Furthermore, all the exams were written by hand and it is very normal to have multiple exams in one day. I personally had 3 exams in one day.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The cultural opportunities, the food and that I found the French people very openminded and helpful.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1) Don't expect any legal-heavy subjects, 2) all exams are written by hand and expect to have multiple exams in one day, and 3) a 40 min - 1 hour train ride to the university from Paris. As the academic level is low, you can expect to have a lot of time to enjoy Paris, which I personally was very happy about.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Sometimes I found the administration at the university quite confused so have patience if you need help with administrative issues.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The most rewarding part was meeting other exchange students from all over the world!

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The greatest challenge was having 3 exams in one day.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
